inputs.notes: net_debt = total_debt - cash_and_investments = 8470 - 80572 = -72102 (net cash). last_fcf is FY2026 actual ($102,718M OCF - $6,042M capex). Balance-sheet items use latest Q1-FY2027 (Apr 26, 2026); cash_and_investments includes $30.2B marketable equity securities. EPS/shares reflect post-2024 10:1 split.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All historical CAGRs (revenue 81%, EPS 114%, FCF 99% over 5yr) reflect the once-in-a-generation AI-infrastructure inflection and are not sustainable terminal rates. Projections therefore use a manually-set decelerating path (35% -> 12% base) rather than any raw CAGR, consistent with the law of large numbers off a $216B revenue / $97B FCF base.

base.description: Secular AI infrastructure growth continues but decelerates from the FY2026 ramp. NVIDIA maintains 80-90% AI GPU share. Hyperscaler CapEx remains elevated but growth normalizes off the very high FY2026 base. FCF margin ~45% sustained.
base.wacc_rationale: 11% reflects large-cap tech beta ~1.5-1.7, risk-free ~4.3%, ERP ~5.5%, plus modest customer-concentration/geopolitical premium

bull.description: Blackwell + Rubin dominance extends; enterprise/sovereign AI accelerates; CUDA moat widens. Hyperscaler CapEx sustains $300B+/yr. Networking scales. Quality premium lowers WACC.
bull.wacc_rationale: 10% for best-case reflecting quality and secular-tailwind premium

bear.description: AI CapEx digestion. Custom silicon (Google TPU, Amazon Trainium, MS Maia) displaces 30-40% of workloads. China controls expand. Revenue plateaus by Y3-Y4 with FCF decline in Y5 as pricing power erodes.
bear.wacc_rationale: 12% for elevated risk: customer concentration, custom-silicon threat, regulatory and geopolitical exposure

sensitivity.notes: Rows = WACC (9%-13%), Cols = Terminal Growth (2.0%-4.0%). Base growth path [35,28,22,16,12]% applied uniformly. Values are intrinsic value per share.

sanity_check.method: Implied multiples at base-case IV vs NVDA 10-year historical trading multiples (Yahoo monthly closes, split-adjusted, vs CSV split-adjusted EPS).
sanity_check.diagnosis: No trigger fired. Base IV $115.72 implies P/E 23.6x on FY2026 actual EPS — below NVDA's 10yr average (~52x) and near its historical minimum (~22x). Base case shows downside (-40.6%), not >100% upside, so no high-upside trigger. Implied P/B and EV/EBITDA are not directly comparable to history because NVDA's book value is structurally low relative to its earnings power (asset-light, large buybacks); the P/E test is the binding one and it passes comfortably.
sanity_check.fix_applied: None. NVDA growth is secular AI-infrastructure driven, not cyclical/agricultural — no peak-FCF mid-cycle swap warranted. WACC of 11% base already prices concentration/geopolitical/custom-silicon risk.
sanity_check.verdict: PASS — model is conservative, not aggressive. The gap between base IV ($115.72) and market ($194.97) reflects the market pricing terminal AI-platform value beyond the explicit 5-year window (CUDA monopoly, $4T+ AI infra TAM by 2030), which a 5-year explicit DCF deliberately excludes. At ~$195 investors pay primarily for terminal platform value carrying material multiple-compression risk.

valuation_philosophy: This is an explicit 5-year FCF DCF off FY2026 actuals ($97B FCF). It deliberately does not capitalize NVDA's full terminal AI-platform optionality, so base IV ($115.72) sits well below market. The base case implies a modest 23.6x P/E on FY2026 EPS — far below NVDA's history — meaning the DCF is conservative. The investment question is not whether NVDA is a good business (it dominates AI compute) but whether the current ~$195 price, embedding a large terminal-value premium, offers an adequate margin of safety. Per the model it does not; bull-case IV (~$185) roughly meets today's price only if hyper-growth persists for years.
